transcript:
Header: 2025-12-12 16:30 UTC — Duration: 1:02:00
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jonah Li (Redwood Perf Eng), Sofia Martinez (Redwood Solutions), Mark Feldman (Aegis ML Eng), Rina Das (Aegis Infra), Omar Khalid (Aegis CTO), Ana Gomez (Aegis QA)

Summary: quick recap at the top, then long technical back-and-forth.

00:00 Alex: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — triage the accuracy reg we saw after the int8+AWQ rollout on the private cluster, validate whether it's quantization or pre/post processing, and plan a layerwise audit.
00:18 Mark: Yeah thanks. to recap from our side — after we switched to the int8-AWQ profile last week we noticed small but measurable drops in rouge and a few hallucinations in the extractor. latency did improve about 18% but some outputs are off.
00:35 Priya: mhm, makes sense. can you share which model variant and the exact bits? was this the 30B fork with the gptq pack applied, or the awq runtime profile?
00:46 Rina: it's the 30b-variant, we tested the "awq-fast" config from Redwood's catalog and it used the int8 weight files we pulled in from the pilot bundle. we did the usual calibration on a 2k-sample set.
00:58 Jonah: quick note — the waveform we saw in perf traces shows kvcache hits are high, but prefix reuse is somewhat different in prod than in the calibration harness. could be a mismatched prompt distribution.
01:12 Alex: right. so three threads: (1) does the accuracy delta correlate to specific layers (layerwise sensitivity), (2) does the runtime fallback mix change inference path under load (i.e., some requests drop to fp16?), and (3) are there infra differences onprem (network egress, CPU offload) affecting quantized inference.
01:28 Ana: we also observed variance across GPUs — A10G vs our onprem H100 nodes. H100 seemed slightly better but not consistent.
01:36 Priya: ok, so first step is a layerwise audit. we'll run per-layer quantization toggles: keep all int8, then flip top-k layers back to fp16/FP8/GPTQ to see where the metric recovers. We suspect final 4 layers and attention output projections are sensitive.
01:52 Mark: sounds good. how invasive is that? we can't ship Frankenstein binaries into our regulated cluster — any runtime impacts?
02:00 Sofia: Redwood runtime supports per-layer precision mixing in both hosted and private runtimes; it can be set via the model config (precision_overrides). for onprem the operator will still need the matching kernels — we provide a small patch that registers mixed-precision kernels, but it does need kernel module permissions on older nodes.
02:19 Rina: that could be the issue — some of our older nodes block unsigned kernel loads. we should be careful.
02:27 Jonah: noted. also worth checking activation quantization vs weight-only. AWQ changes weight representations and sometimes adds an activation scaling step which can interact poorly with kv cache since cached outputs were quantized differently. sometimes the kvcache ends up with mismatched scale factors, leading to subtle drift.
02:47 Alex: good point. Ana, can you confirm whether your kvcache is using the legacy serialization (we call it v1) or the compact v2?
02:55 Ana: it's v1. we didn't switch the serialization in the update.
03:01 Priya: that's a useful lead — mixing AWQ weight quant with an older kvcache encoding can definitely introduce numeric mismatch in recombined past tokens. as a test we can enable runtime fallback that reads kvcache and re-scales on deserialization, or serve requests with cache disabled to see delta.
03:18 Mark: disabling cache will blow latency though. but for a bench it makes sense.
03:25 Alex: agreed. bench plan: baseline (current int8+awq, kvcache v1), run with kvcache disabled, run with per-layer fp16 overrides on the last 6 layers, run with GPTQ weight variant for the same model, run with FP8 for last N layers, measure rouge/accuracy + latency P50/P95 and cost.
03:48 Rina: on the infra side we also need to validate that we didn't have quantization happening at build-time with different RNG seeds causing calibration mismatch — our CI pipeline does model conversion and sometimes the quant table differs micro-ly.
04:03 Jonah: we'll add a deterministic seed and checksum the quant tables. also will collect per-layer L2 error vs float32 as part of the audit.
04:12 Mark: what's the quickest way to get per-layer sensitivity metrics? we have limited windows on the private cluster.
04:20 Priya: Redwood SEs have a script that iteratively forces layers to fp32/FP16/FP8 and runs a small eval set — it spits out delta metrics and a CSV. I can run it remotely if you provide the model bundle path and a short eval set (50 prompts).
04:35 Alex: action item for Mark to upload 50 canonical prompts and expected outputs. Priya will run the audit in your environment.
04:45 Ana: one more caveat — for onprem we have HSM-backed keys and a tight KMS integration; we want to avoid exporting models or weight files unencrypted. is SE going to run without pulling weights out?
04:58 Sofia: yes — Redwood can run the audit tooling inside your VPC. SE will deploy a temporary job via your private control plane, we won't exfiltrate weights. for debugging we may request hashes, but not raw dumps unless you permit.
05:14 Omar: good. and what about fallback policies in runtime for production? we want graceful degradation: if a request triggers an accuracy regression, can we fall back to a higher-precision path per-request?
05:25 Jonah: runtime supports per-request precision hints; we can tag high-confidence prompts to use int8, and lower-confidence to prefer fp16/FP8. the routing adds ~2ms overhead for flag evaluation, but it's small relative to token generation. the main cost is memory for keeping both weight variants resident or on quick swap.
05:46 Priya: there are two runtime fallback patterns: (A) on-the-fly per-request precision override (cheap to implement, needs both kernels available), and (B) canary routing — send N% of traffic to a higher-precision model variant in a different pool. Onprem canary is heavier operationally but less risky.
06:04 Mark: we prefer (B) for production; (A) for immediate mitigation during the audit.
06:10 Alex: noted. other tests — we'll run mixed-precision on H100 vs A10G to see hardware sensitivity. sometimes INT8 on A10G maps to faster kernels but shows worse accuracy compared to H100 FP8 fast paths.
06:26 Rina: our fleet mixes A10G + H100; we need recommendations on which hardware to pin for the production pool.
06:33 Jonah: pin H100 for high-accuracy tier and A10G for cost-sensitive tier. Redwood's smart routing can route by latency SLOs and cost budgets.
06:42 Ana: can you share the benchmark harness and scripts? we want to reproduce exactly.
06:48 Priya: yes — we'll share a tarball with the audit script, the CSV outputs format, and a docker job to run inside your cluster. also provide a small perf harness to measure P50/P95 and token/sec.
06:59 Alex: ok let's recap next steps — Priya run layerwise audit inside Aegis cluster, Mark provide prompts, Alex send SOW and pricing, Jonah will prepare benchmarking machines and kernel checksum scripts.
07:10 Mark: timeline check — we can provision a bench window on 12/18 and 12/19. is that acceptable?
07:16 Alex: yes, we'll aim for 12/18 first run and iterate.
07:21 Omar: one last question about data residency — since we run the audit inside the VPC are logs being exported to Redwood? we need audit logs to remain local.
07:31 Sofia: by default logs are ephemeral and stored in your stack; we can enable or disable upload. we'll keep them local unless you explicitly allow.
07:40 Ana: thanks. that addresses the main privacy concerns.
07:44 Alex: great. any other quick questions?
07:47 Rina: minor — did anyone check whether the inference container used cudnn vs custom kernels? that affects int8 performance and numeric stability.
07:55 Jonah: yes, it's a mix. our runtime chooses kernels at startup depending on CUDA/cuDNN versions. we'll include kernel mapping in the report so you can see which kernels were active in each bench.
08:07 Mark: perfect. thanks everyone.

Wrap / Recap (short):
- Layerwise sensitivity audit to find sensitive layers (Priya).
- Bench comparisons: int8+awq vs gptq vs fp8 last layers vs per-layer mix (Jonah/Priya).
- Kernel and kvcache serialization checks (Jonah/Ana).
- Pricing/SOW & scheduling (Alex).

Links mentioned: Redwood audit script (link: /redwood/internal/audit/layerwise-runner.sh), private bench job template (link: /redwood/templates/onprem/bench-job.yaml), SOW draft (link: drive.redwood/sow-drafts/aegis-int8-pilot.pdf)

End of meeting.
